findings.summary: `allowed_bots` hardcodes the bot login "yorkie-agent" with nothing tying it to the App actually configured via AGENT_APP_ID; if the slug differs the allow-list silently fails to match and every fix run still aborts
findings.evidence: Both new lines read `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-review-panel.yml:413, agent-iterate-ci.yml:160). The App identity is supplied entirely by repo secrets (`app-id: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_ID }}`, agent-review-panel.yml:373), and the setup runbook explicitly allows either the Claude GitHub App or "a dedicated app installed on the repo" (docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:75-77). No file in the repo asserts the installed App's slug is `yorkie-agent` (grep for `yorkie-agent` matches only these two new lines). The initiating actor login for a workflow_run from an App push is `<app-slug>[bot]`, so if the configured App is anything else (e.g. the Claude GitHub App → `claude[bot]`), the allow-list does not match, claude-code-action still refuses the bot-initiated run, the fix job fails, and the loop only pages a human instead of iterating. `actions/create-github-app-token` exposes an `app-slug` output that would make this derived rather than guessed.

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` may not be a recognized input at the pinned claude-code-action commit; an unknown `with:` key only warns, so the workflow would look fixed while the bot block persists
findings.evidence: The action is pinned to the immutable commit `anthropics/claude-code-action@af0559ee4f514d1ef21826982bed13f7edc3c35e # v1` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:151, agent-review-panel.yml:404). GitHub Actions does not fail a job for an input the action does not declare — it emits an "Unexpected input" warning and drops it. If `allowed_bots` was added to the action after that pinned commit, the intended unblocking is a no-op and both loops keep failing exactly as before, with the only visible change being the new `stalled` page. The repo contains no vendored copy of the action to verify the input list against (agent-implement.yml:221 even notes "Re-check input names ... when bumping"), so this cannot be confirmed from the tree.
searchedFor: grep for allowed_bots in repo (only the 2 new lines)

findings.summary: agent-iterate-ci has no paging net for a failed fixer step, so the same failure mode the review-panel diff now catches still stalls the CI-fix loop silently
findings.evidence: The review-panel diff adds `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` to `stalled` precisely because "claude-code-action refusing a bot-initiated run ... so no fix was pushed and no fresh cycle starts" (agent-review-panel.yml:441-444). agent-iterate-ci.yml has the identical shape — the `Run Claude Code` step at line 147 is the last step of the only job, and there is no `always()`/`if: failure()` step or downstream job that comments or applies `agent:needs-human-review` when it errors. The in-job guard only pages when `failedCi >= max` (lines 102-111), and since a failed fixer pushes nothing, CI never re-runs, `failedCi` never grows, and no further `workflow_run` event is produced: the branch is abandoned with no human notification.
searchedFor: read whole .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml for always()/failure() steps or extra jobs
grep for agent:needs-human-review in the repo

findings.summary: The `stalled` comment text hard-asserts "The review-panel job failed to complete" / "the automated panel did not produce verdicts", which is factually wrong for the newly added fix-failure (and existing promote-failure) trigger
findings.evidence: The trigger set now includes `needs.promote.result == 'failure' || needs.fix.result == 'failure'` (lines 459-460), but the only comment body posted (line 479) states the panel failed to produce verdicts. In the fix-failure case the panel succeeded and produced verdicts; the fixer errored. The human paged is handed an incorrect diagnosis, sending them to the wrong job.

findings.summary: `stalled` posts its paging comment unconditionally with no `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` latch check, so it can duplicate a page the fix guard already posted
findings.evidence: The fix job's guard latches on the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` sentinel before acting (lines 314-324), but the `stalled` job posts the same sentinel comment with no prior listComments check (lines 477-480). With `fix` newly in the trigger set, a run where the guard already paged and a later step in the same or a subsequent run reds the job yields repeated 🛑 comments on the PR. Low blast radius, but the latch that exists elsewhere is missing here.

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` disables claude-code-action's actor (non-bot) guard on the two secret-bearing, contents:write, Bash-enabled agent jobs, making a fully human-free execution path for prompts built from untrusted branch output
findings.evidence: Both new lines (`agent-iterate-ci.yml:160`, `agent-review-panel.yml:413`) turn off the action's built-in refusal of bot-initiated runs. That guard was the last human-in-the-loop signal on these jobs: `iterate` runs with `environment: agent` (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN + AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY), a minted App token with contents:write (line 154), and `--allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep"` (line 176). The prompt it feeds that agent is `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` (line 165), which is `scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs` output, which embeds `failureSummary` verbatim (summarize-ci.mjs:92-97) from `.harness-reports/*.json` written by `scripts/verify-self.mjs:143` as `extractFailureSummary(output)` — i.e. raw stdout/stderr of test/build commands defined by the *branch under review*. Attack: any text that lands in a failing lane's output on an `agent/` branch (a test name, console.log, snapshot diff — content the author agent itself derived from an attacker-authored issue body) becomes instructions in an autonomous, unattended Bash+push agent session. Previously each such invocation needed a non-bot initiating actor; now the bot's own push closes the loop with nobody watching. The residual mitigations are `environment: agent` required reviewers (optional, not enforced in-repo) and the MAX_ATTEMPTS bound, which limits volume, not blast radius. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:436-446 says early phases SHOULD keep a human approval on secret-bearing runs; this change removes the last automatic one, so the environment protection rule must be verified as configured before merge.

findings.summary: Bot allow-list also lists the bare login `yorkie-agent` (no `[bot]` suffix), widening the allow-list into the ordinary GitHub user namespace
findings.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (also agent-iterate-ci.yml:160). A GitHub App's actor login is always `<slug>[bot]`; the second entry can only ever match a plain user/organization account named `yorkie-agent`. If claude-code-action matches the allow-list by login string without independently asserting `actor.type == 'Bot'` (its input is documented as a list of bot usernames), then any actor with that login is allow-listed — a login that is registerable by anyone on github.com if it is not already held by this project. Exploitation still requires push access to an `agent/` branch of the base repo (the fork gate at agent-review-panel.yml:38 holds), so impact is limited to widening the trusted set beyond the intended single App; drop the un-suffixed entry so the allow-list names exactly one bot identity. Note also that nothing else in the repo references the slug `yorkie-agent` (grep across the tree returns only these two lines), so the intended identity is unverifiable from source.
searchedFor: read .github/workflows/agent-implement.yml, agent-review-reply.yml for the App identity

findings.summary: GITHUB_OUTPUT heredoc delimiter injection: untrusted lane output can break out of the fixed `HARNESS_EOF` delimiter and define arbitrary step outputs — a path this change makes autonomously reachable
findings.evidence: Lines 141-145 write `summary<<HARNESS_EOF` then the raw stdout of `summarize-ci.mjs` then `HARNESS_EOF` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The content is unsanitized branch-produced text (summarize-ci.mjs:97 prints `failureSummary`, captured from lane process output at scripts/verify-self.mjs:143). A failing lane whose output contains a line consisting of `HARNESS_EOF` terminates the heredoc early; every subsequent line is then parsed by the runner as a new `key=value` / `key<<DELIM` output assignment for the `diag` step, letting branch-controlled text define step outputs and truncate/replace the diagnosis actually shown to the agent. The delimiter is a fixed, publicly known constant rather than a per-run random value, which is the standard mitigation. Pre-existing lines, but the `allowed_bots` change is what makes this step run without a human-initiated trigger.

findings.summary: Paged-latch lookup in the iterate attempts guard is unpaginated (first 30 comments only), unlike the review-panel guard which was explicitly fixed to paginate
findings.evidence: `github.rest.issues.listComments` at lines 95-98 is called without `github.paginate`/`per_page`, so the `<!-- agent-paged -->` sentinel is only searched in the first page of comments; the equivalent latch in agent-review-panel.yml:323 paginates precisely because "an iterating PR easily exceeds 30 comments". The agent holds issues:write, so it also controls comment volume. Here the failedCi>=max branch still trips, so the loop does not actually proceed past the bound — the effect is duplicate pages rather than a bypass — but the latch is a loop-bound control and should be read exhaustively for the same reason the panel one is.
searchedFor: read both guard scripts in agent-iterate-ci.yml and agent-review-panel.yml

The action is pinned to the immutable SHA anthropics/claude-code-action@af0559ee4f514d1ef21826982bed13f7edc3c35e # v1 at agent-iterate-ci.yml:151 and agent-review-panel.yml:404, and allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent" is passed under with: at agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413. The underlying risk is unverifiable offline rather than disproved, and unverifiable is not refutable, so the finding stays on the gate. Repo-wide, the only two workflow_run consumers both listen on workflows: ["CI"] (agent-iterate-ci.yml:19-20, agent-review-panel.yml:19-20) — nothing keys off "Agent Iterate (CI)". The review-panel `stalled` net (agent-review-panel.yml:448-460) cannot cover it: it requires workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' while the iterate arm only fires on conclusion == 'failure' (agent-iterate-ci.yml:40), and its needs: [deps, review-panel, promote, fix] are jobs in that other file. verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed chain is present and reachable. `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` exists verbatim at agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413, and the workflows' own comments (155-159, 408-412) state its purpose is to bypass claude-code-action's refusal of bot-initiated runs. Both jobs are secret-bearing and write-capable: environment: agent (iterate:45), contents: write (iterate:24), App private key (60), CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (153), minted App token as github_token (154), and --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep" (176; panel:432). The untrusted data path is real: the prompt interpolates steps.diag.outputs.summary (165) from summarize-ci.mjs, which embeds failureSummary verbatim in an unescaped fenced block (summarize-ci.mjs:92-98); that value is extractFailureSummary(output) at verify-self.mjs:143, where output is raw stdout/stderr of branch-defined lane commands (verify-self.mjs:31-53, 55-66). The iterate prompt lacks any "data not instructions" framing, unlike the panel prompt at agent-review-panel.yml:415-417. Attacker-influenceable text can plausibly reach that output because agent-implement.yml:152-161 has the agent read an arbitrary-author issue body via gh. No refutation ground applies: the surviving gates (AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED, fork/branch checks at 38-42, attempts bound at 68-112) constrain who triggers and how often, not whether injected text reaches the agent prompt, so `already-guarded` fails; the lines are exactly as described, so `not-present` fails; and prompt injection into a Bash-enabled agent holding an OAuth token and contents:write App token is in-lane for the security rubric, so `out-of-scope` fails. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:441-446 independently states early phases SHOULD keep a human approval on secret-bearing runs, and the only remaining mitigation (environment required reviewers) is repo-settings state not verifiable from the tree.
